stories.title: Japanese Restaurant Udon Shin to Open First NYC Restaurant at 37 West 17th Street
stories.excerpt: Udon Shin, a popular Japanese restaurant with only two other U.S. locations, is gearing up to open its first New York City eatery, Commercial Observer has learned. Udon Shin has signed a 10-year, 2,500-square-foot lease at 37 West 17th Street in Manhattan’s Flatiron District, according to tenant broker Aaron Gavios of Gavios Realty Group. Asking rent was $30,000 per month for the space previously occupied by now-closed Italian restaurant Basta Pasta. Udon Shin originated in Tokyo but recently opened its first U.S. location in Mesa, Ariz., where its lines are “out the door,” Gavios said. Another U.S. spot is coming soon to Utah. “We are expecting long waits and long lines when Udon Shin opens here in the Flatiron District. It should be the latest Japanese foodie sensation,” Gavios said. Landlord the Moinian Group was represented in this deal by Samuel Chera and David Green of KSR. “The continued interest from exciting international restaurant concepts speaks to the strength of Manhattan’s retail market and the demand for quality locations,” Green said to CO. “We believe Udon Shin will be a great addition to the neighborhood and look forward to seeing its success.” Built in 1900, 37 West 17th Street is a seven-story office and commercial property two blocks west of Union Square Park and about six blocks south of the landmark Flatiron Building. Other tenants include acupuncture clinic the Yinova Center and British music producer De Wolfe Music USA. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Udon Shin signs 10-year, 2,500-SF lease at $30K/month in Manhattan Flatiron District
Japanese restaurant expanding from 2 U.S. locations; Mesa location reports high demand
Ground-floor retail activation in Flatiron signals continued foodie-driven foot traffic demand
stories.summary: Udon Shin, a Tokyo-origin Japanese restaurant with only two U.S. locations, has leased 2,500 square feet at 37 West 17th Street in Manhattan's Flatiron District on a 10-year term at $30,000/month. The space replaces the now-closed Basta Pasta. The Moinian Group landlord and broker Aaron Gavios expect strong customer traffic, with comparisons drawn to the Mesa, Arizona location's success.
stories.impact: Minor relevance to multifamily development. Ground-floor retail leasing signals Flatiron District remains economically vibrant, supporting mixed-use development feasibility and residential asset appeal in the submarket, but this is a single restaurant lease, not a material demand driver for apartment construction.

stories.title: Digital Communications Firm Next 15 Signs 6K-SF Lease at 78 Crosby Street
stories.excerpt: A U.K.-based digital communications firm has leased the third floor of a SoHo office building, Commercial Observer has learned. Next Fifteen Communications Group, also known as Next 15, signed a 6,350-square-foot lease at Milkystar’s 78 Crosby Street, the same building occupied by betting platform Polymarket, according to landlord broker Judson CRE. It will be the artificial intelligence-driven company’s first New York City office. Judson CRE declined to disclose the length of the lease but said the asking rent in the space was $75 per square foot. Nicholas Judson, Wendy McDonald and Crosby Matthews of Judson CRE negotiated on behalf of the landlord. Brandon DeGraff and Jimmy Giattino with Cushman & Wakefield represented the tenant when the deal closed in the last two weeks, but have since gone to work for JLL. C&W declined to comment while JLL did not immediately respond to request for comment. Polymarket moved into the SoHo building between Spring and Prince streets in 2023, occupying the fifth floor before expanding to 12,700 square feet on the fourth floor in August under its parent company, Blockratize. Both were founded by 28-year-old CEO and billionaire Shayne Coplan. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Next Fifteen Communications (UK AI firm) leases 6,350 SF at 78 Crosby Street, SoHo
First NYC office for digital comms company; $75/SF asking rent in creative office space
AI-driven tenant signals SoHo office market attracting specialized tech talent clusters
stories.summary: Next Fifteen Communications Group, a U.K.-based AI-driven digital communications firm, has signed a 6,350-square-foot lease on the third floor of 78 Crosby Street in SoHo. The asking rent was $75 per square foot. This marks the company's first New York City office, and the building also houses crypto betting platform Polymarket.
stories.impact: Modest signal for Manhattan multifamily demand. AI and fintech tenant relocations to SoHo suggest growing tech-talent in-migration to central Manhattan submarkets; this could drive incremental young-professional demand for nearby residential, especially in walkable downtown locations like SoHo and Nolita, but the office market is still in transition and single-tenant leases do not indicate broad-based employment influx.

stories.title: Slatt Capital Arranges Life Company Refi for Palm Springs Retail
stories.excerpt: Slatt Capital arranged a $12,000,000 refinance for Gene Autry Plaza, a 60,629-square-foot multi-tenant retail property located in Palm Springs. Built in 2009, the property was financed through a life insurance company with a five-year term and 30-year amortization schedule. The permanent loan is structured as partial recourse. Michael Kaplan, Slatt Capital’s president, led the transaction on behalf of the unnamed borrower, with support from Andrew Friedeberg. Upland-based 1st Commercial Realty Group provides property management services for the asset, which is occupied by a mix of tenants including food, fitness and health operators. “Gene Autry Plaza checks a lot of boxes for lenders: a grocery-anchored center in an affluent market, with the daily-needs tenants that drive consistent foot traffic regardless of the economic cycle,” said Kaplan. “Life companies value that kind of durable, necessity-driven income, and the property’s location next to the Palm Springs Airport and the Gene Autry Business District adds to its appeal.” The post Slatt Capital Arranges Life Company Refi for Palm Springs Retail appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: $12M life-company refi for 60,629-SF retail (Gene Autry Plaza) in Palm Springs
Grocery-anchored center with food, fitness, health tenants; strong necessity-driven income
Life insurers favor durable retail income; proximity to airport and business district adds appeal
stories.summary: Slatt Capital arranged a $12 million refinance for Gene Autry Plaza, a 60,629-square-foot multi-tenant retail property built in 2009 in Palm Springs. The loan is structured through a life insurance company with a five-year term and 30-year amortization. The property is anchored by grocery and daily-need tenants and benefits from proximity to Palm Springs Airport and the Gene Autry Business District.
stories.impact: Low relevance to multifamily development. Life-company refi of necessity-driven retail signals stable NOI in Palm Springs retail; however, this is a capital markets event in retail, not a signal of residential demand. No direct implication for apartment development pipeline or demand drivers in the Palm Springs market.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Acquisition Loan for Fort Greene Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: CBRE Capital Markets arranged a $12-million acquisition loan for the purchase of 680 Fulton St., a mixed-use property in Brooklyn’s Fort Greene neighborhood. The Debt & Structured Finance team of Shamir Seidman, Judah Hammer and Jeff Feldman secured the financing on behalf of Z+G Property Group through Santander. The five-year loan represents approximately 70% loan-to-value and features an initial period of interest-only payments. “This financing supports the acquisition of an excellent mixed-use asset in one of Brooklyn’s most desirable residential neighborhoods,” said Seidman. “The property’s historic character, established retail tenancy and strong residential appeal generated significant lender interest, resulting in an attractive financing structure for the borrower.” Known as The Portland, 680-686 Fulton St. is a four-story, neo-Renaissance mixed-use building featuring a limestone façade and dating back to approximately 1900. The property includes ground-floor retail space anchored by Greenlight Bookstore and Yours Truly stationery shop, with residential apartments above ranging from studio to two-bedroom units. The post CBRE Arranges Acquisition Loan for Fort Greene Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE arranges $12M acquisition loan (70% LTV) for 680 Fulton St. mixed-use in Fort Greene, Brooklyn
Four-story historic building with ground-floor retail (Greenlight Bookstore, Yours Truly) and residential units
Interest-only initial period; established retail tenancy and historic character attract lender confidence
stories.summary: CBRE Capital Markets secured a $12 million acquisition loan (70% LTV) through Santander for 680 Fulton Street in Brooklyn's Fort Greene neighborhood. The property, known as The Portland, is a circa-1900 four-story neo-Renaissance mixed-use building with ground-floor retail and residential apartments (studio to two-bedroom). The five-year loan features an initial interest-only period.
stories.impact: Positive signal for Fort Greene multifamily fundamentals. Lender willingness to finance historic mixed-use residential in Fort Greene at 70% LTV with favorable terms (interest-only initial period) indicates strong neighborhood demand and asset stability. This supports developer appetite to acquire or build residential in Fort Greene, as the neighborhood continues to attract capital and maintain healthy rent growth and occupancy.

bullets: Cushman & Wakefield CIO Campbell advises firms to start with 10 high-impact AI use cases, then scale
Unframe AI platform converts enterprise needs into production-ready solutions in days
Focus on high-impact domains with cleanest data to build foundational AI layers

Indirectly, if multifamily operators and developers adopt this phased AI approach (e.g., targeting leasing, marketing, operations analytics first), it could improve underwriting accuracy and asset management, but this is not a market signal affecting demand, supply, capital availability, or construction costs.

stories.title: Ross Stores Takes 115K SF for West Coast Merchandising Hub
stories.excerpt: Discount retailer Ross Stores has signed a 115,000-square-foot lease in one of the largest recent office commitments in Downtown Los Angeles, Commercial Observer can first report. The company will relocate its West Coast merchandising hub from Downtown’s central business district to about 110,000 square feet of creative office space and 5,000 square feet of exclusive rooftop space at the campus known as Row DTLA, according to the landlord, Atlas Capital Group. The new location will support Ross’ vendor collaboration and its ongoing nationwide retail expansion. Downtown L.A.’s office market is still grappling with high vacancy and a long-running flight toward newer or highly amenitized space, typically in submarkets such as Century City. Rather than leaving Downtown altogether, Ross is shifting from a traditional CBD setting to a sprawling adaptive-reuse campus in Downtown’s Arts District and near the Fashion District. “Finding the right space is about much more than square footage,” Wade Haddad, senior vice president of corporate properties at Ross, said in a statement. The company more commonly known as Ross Dress for Less also deepens Row DTLA’s concentration of fashion and apparel tenants. Pistola Denim recently signed a 17,900-square-foot lease at the property for its creative team, relocating from warehouse and distribution space in Vernon just outside L.A. Also, Fashionphile leased 32,300 square feet last year for a flagship location combining retail, office, operations, authentication and storage functions. Other fashion tenants at the complex include Adidas, Wilson and Revolve, which recently renewed a 48,000-square-foot lease. Row DTLA spans 32 acres and occupies a collection of former industrial buildings dating to the 1920s Los Angeles Terminal Market. The campus was redeveloped and reopened in 2017, and now includes offices, restaurants, retailers, wellness operators and event space. JLL’s Jaclyn Ward, Cassie Trosclair and Sarah Hancock represented Row D
bullets: Ross Stores leases 115,000 SF at Row DTLA (Arts/Fashion District), relocating West Coast merchandising hub
Shift from traditional CBD office to adaptive-reuse campus signals retail tenant workplace innovation
Downtown LA office market still elevated vacancy; Ross staying in DTLA but moving to creative space
stories.summary: Discount retailer Ross Stores has signed a 115,000-square-foot lease (110,000 SF creative office plus 5,000 SF rooftop) at Row DTLA, an adaptive-reuse campus in Downtown Los Angeles' Arts District near the Fashion District. The company is relocating its West Coast merchandising hub from Downtown's central business district. The move reflects Ross' vendor collaboration needs and nationwide retail expansion.
stories.impact: Weak signal for multifamily. While Ross' relocation to Row DTLA shows creative-office demand and adaptive-reuse appeal, it does not represent new employment or population growth—it is a lateral corporate move within DTLA. Downtown LA office remains challenged with high vacancy. Multifamily developers should note that DTLA's residential appeal is tied to Arts District gentrification and mixed-use revitalization (like Row DTLA), not broad office-job growth; focus construction on loft-style, walkable residential near retail/creative anchors, not office-proximate conventional apartment development.

stories.title: Related Beal Acquires Back Bay’s Historic Motor Mart Garage
stories.excerpt: Related Beal, in partnership with Freeport Equity, has acquired Motor Mart Garage, a mixed-use parking and retail asset in Boston’s Back Bay neighborhood. Terms were not disclosed. The seller was CIM Group, which acquired the historic property in 2016 and initially planned to redevelop it as residential. CBRE Capital Markets brought the century-old asset to market this past January, according to published reports. “We are pleased to add the iconic Motor Mart Garage in Boston’s Back Bay to our portfolio,” said Kimberly Sherman Stamler, president of Related Beal. “Motor Mart sits at the heart of a neighborhood we have been investing in for many years and holds great possibility for future residential and commercial development.” Located at 201 Stuart St., the garage was fully restored in 1999. Related Beal intends to continue operating the existing 1,037-stall parking garage and ground-floor retail while exploring future residential and mixed-use development with the City of Boston and neighborhood stakeholders. Photo courtesy of BPDL. The post Related Beal Acquires Back Bay’s Historic Motor Mart Garage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Related Beal and Freeport Equity acquire Motor Mart Garage (1,037 stalls + ground-floor retail) in Boston Back Bay
CIM Group sold after acquiring in 2016 with initial residential redevelopment plan; Related Beal exploring mixed-use residential
Historic parking garage at 201 Stuart St.; Related Beal will operate existing asset while planning future residential
stories.summary: Related Beal, in partnership with Freeport Equity, acquired Motor Mart Garage, a century-old mixed-use parking and retail asset in Boston's Back Bay neighborhood, from CIM Group. The property features a fully restored 1,037-stall parking garage and ground-floor retail. Related Beal intends to continue current operations while exploring future residential and mixed-use development with city and neighborhood stakeholders.
stories.impact: Moderate signal for Boston Back Bay multifamily. Related Beal's acquisition and stated intention to develop residential above/integrated with parking and retail suggests confidence in Back Bay's continued residential demand and regulatory environment. The back-and-forth (CIM's initial residential plan → parking focus → Related Beal's renewed residential exploration) reflects developer conviction in long-term neighborhood value; indicates a potential pipeline project that could add meaningful units to a constrained, high-value Boston submarket.

stories.title: Old Denver Brick Plant Converting to Warehouse Campus
stories.excerpt: The General Shale brick plant at 3003 S. Platte River Drive in Denver may transform into a four-building warehouse distribution campus. The 50.5-acre industrial site northwest may turn into 542,784 square feet of warehousing and office space. The Denver Business Journal reports that the property has been a brick plant for decades and was formerly owned by Robinson Brick Co., founded in 1880 in Denver. It’s not clear what the brick company’s role will be going forward. Ryan Cos. submitted the documents to the city. Ryan Cos. develops, designs, builds and manages properties. The redevelopment is intended to provide flexible, modern industrial space capable of accommodating a range of office/warehouse, distribution, logistics, and light industrial uses. Development of the General Share brick plant would occur in two phases, with two warehouses totaling about 94,000 square feet each being built in phase one. Phase two would include one building proposed at 206,136 square feet and another at 138,934 square feet. The post Old Denver Brick Plant Converting to Warehouse Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: General Shale brick plant (50.5 acres, Denver) redeveloping into 542,784 SF warehouse/office campus
Two-phase development: Phase 1 = 188,000 SF (two buildings), Phase 2 = 345,070 SF (two buildings)
Ryan Cos. developer; flexible modern industrial for distribution, logistics, light industrial, office uses
stories.summary: The former General Shale brick plant at 3003 S. Platte River Drive in Denver (50.5 acres) is converting to a four-building warehouse distribution campus totaling 542,784 square feet. Developer Ryan Cos. submitted plans for a two-phase project: Phase 1 will include two ~94,000-SF warehouses; Phase 2 will add buildings of 206,136 SF and 138,934 SF. The campus will accommodate office/warehouse, distribution, logistics, and light industrial tenants.
stories.impact: Indirect signal for Denver metro multifamily. Large industrial redevelopment in northwest Denver signals continued logistics/warehouse demand and employment growth in Denver's industrial submarkets. This could drive worker in-migration and increase demand for workforce housing near industrial nodes. However, developers should note: this is supply-side industrial growth, not residential; it will drive demand for lower-cost, transit-accessible multifamily near distribution centers, not luxury downtown residential.

stories.title: Bank OZK Provides $133M Construction Loan for Culver City, Calif., Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: The development firms behind a 344-unit mixed-use project set for Culver City, Calif., have secured $132.7 million in construction financing from Bank OZK. A joint venture of Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners said it will use the loan to build the six-story project, which will include 52 affordable units as well as 2,000 square feet of retail and 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space. It will also include two floors of residential amenities and 500 parking spaces. KFA Architecture is designing the project, called ElevenOneEleven, that will rise on a 3.4-acre site at 11111 Jefferson Boulevard, near Downtown Culver City and Playa Vista in neighboring L.A. Construction is expected to begin before the end of the year. Berkadia’s Louis Friedel and Keith Rosso arranged the financing on behalf of the developers. The financing adds another sizable Southern California construction loan to Bank OZK’s stable. The lender said it originated $38.75 billion in new commercial real estate loans in total during the five years ended June 30. “Securing construction financing in today’s environment speaks to the strength of the sponsorship and the fundamentals behind this project,” Friedel said in a statement. “Los Angeles County continues to add new apartment supply at a relatively measured pace, while demand is projected to outpace deliveries. Culver City is particularly well positioned, with a deep employment base, strong connectivity and immediate access to the Westside.” Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bank OZK provides $132.7M construction loan for 344-unit mixed-use project (ElevenOneEleven) in Culver City, Calif.
Includes 52 affordable units, 2,000 SF retail, 17,520 SF public outdoor space, 500 parking spaces
Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners joint venture; construction begins by year-end; 3.4-acre site near Playa Vista
stories.summary: A joint venture of Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners secured $132.7 million in construction financing from Bank OZK for ElevenOneEleven, a 344-unit mixed-use residential project in Culver City, California. The six-story building will include 52 affordable units, 2,000 square feet of retail, 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space, two residential amenity floors, and 500 parking spaces on a 3.4-acre site at 11111 Jefferson Boulevard. Construction is expected to begin before year-end.
stories.impact: Positive for Southern California multifamily supply and financing accessibility. Bank OZK's commitment of $132.7M for a mixed-use project with significant affordable component signals lender confidence in Culver City/Playa Vista submarket and mixed-use typologies. The affordable-unit inclusion suggests regulatory support and possibly public financing layers (likely LIHTC, NACA, or local incentives). This project adds 344 units to LA's constrained supply; developers should note Culver City is attracting institutional financing and mixed-use is the dominant typology—expect continued competition for infill land near employment clusters (Playa Vista tech corridor).

stories.title: North County Apartment Duo Trades for $37M
stories.excerpt: Colliers finalized the sale of a two-property multifamily portfolio in Fallbrook totaling approximately $37 million in value. The portfolio included Amberwood Apartments, a 133-unit community at 923 Alturas Rd., which sold for $24.25 million, and Rosewood Apartments, a 73-unit apartment community at 338 Ammunition Rd., which sold for $12.4 million. EVPts Shane Shafer and Brian Anderson represented the sellers, Amber Creek Associates LTD and Rosewood Associates LTD, respectively, in the transactions. Among the larger multifamily investment opportunities traded in the Fallbrook market in recent years, these properties generated significant investor interest due to their established operations, desirable locations, and long-term value-add potential. The transactions reflect continued demand for well-positioned apartment communities throughout North San Diego County. “Opportunistic multifamily investments throughout Southern California continue to attract strong investor interest, driven by the region’s constrained housing supply and persistent supply-demand imbalance, which continue to support positive long-term fundamentals,” said Shafer. “Amberwood and Rosewood each offered characteristics buyers continue to prioritize, including value-add potential, strong underlying fundamentals, and opportunities to enhance value through proactive ownership and operational improvements.” The post North County Apartment Duo Trades for $37M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Colliers finalizes sale of two-property multifamily portfolio in Fallbrook, San Diego County for $37M total
Amberwood Apartments (133 units) sold for $24.25M; Rosewood Apartments (73 units) sold for $12.4M
Buyers prioritize value-add potential, established operations, long-term fundamentals in North San Diego County
stories.summary: Colliers finalized the sale of a two-property multifamily portfolio in Fallbrook totaling approximately $37 million. Amberwood Apartments (133 units at 923 Alturas Road) sold for $24.25 million, and Rosewood Apartments (73 units at 338 Ammunition Road) sold for $12.4 million. The sales reflect strong investor demand for established multifamily with value-add potential in North San Diego County.
stories.impact: Positive market signal for San Diego County multifamily fundamentals. Colliers and broker commentary emphasize constrained housing supply and supply-demand imbalance driving investor appetite for existing multifamily in North County. This activity signals cap rates are attractive enough to warrant portfolio acquisitions; indicates sustained rent growth and operational stability justify value-add investment. Developers should view Fallbrook and North County as submarkets where new supply may attract builder interest, though land availability and entitlement timelines remain key constraints.
